decisions.statement: A level is a command page or a namespace page.
The page types the levels are read under are handed in.
What a level states is read from what the index carries for that page type.
Every level of those page types is read at once rather than one at a time.
The levels of one checkout are read once and held for the rest of the run.
A part names a level by that level's page type and that level's slug.
A part naming no level answers with none.
A slug more than one page of a page type carries answers with each of them.
A level's name is the name its page states, or its slug where none is stated.
Nothing here joins words into a slug.

definition: the levels of the command tree, as the index carries what each level states
